articles.title: Samson, Dhir Power India to Record 226 Chase Against New Zealand
articles.excerpt: Sanju Samson made 67 off 33 balls and Naman Dhir finished unbeaten on 42 off 15 as India reached 230 for 6 in 19.4 overs in Christchurch, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the first T20I.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian fans in New Zealand and worldwide, India's record chase in Christchurch opened the five-match series with a statement win built on aggressive opening batting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Suvarna Raj Wins Discus Gold as India Reach 15 Golds at Asian Para Games
articles.excerpt: On day four in Aichi-Nagoya, Suvarna Raj's 15.66-metre throw won the women's F54 discus, Swati Chaudhary took archery silver and Manisha Ramadass and Pramod Bhagat took badminton bronze, moving India to 65 medals.
articles.nri_angle: India's para-athletes moved to fifth in the medal table on day four, a campaign diaspora sports readers have followed since Nishad Kumar's five-gold day on October 21.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anahat Singh Stuns Eight-Time World Champion El Sherbini at Silicon Valley Open
articles.excerpt: The 18-year-old Indian beat top seed and world No. 3 Nour El Sherbini 11-8, 11-8, 11-7 in 30 minutes in Redwood City to reach the quarter-finals of the $143,500 PSA Gold event.
articles.image_caption: Anahat Singh raises a fist in celebration during a squash match. The Indian beat eight-time world champion Nour El Sherbini in straight games at the Silicon Valley Open to reach the quarter-finals.
articles.nri_angle: Anahat Singh's win came in Redwood City, California, on the PSA tour in the US, ahead of squash's Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028 — a breakthrough US-based diaspora audiences can follow in person and on tour.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Complete 3-0 Zimbabwe Sweep as Harmanpreet's 91 Seals 92-Run Win

articles.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur, India's captain. Her 91 sealed a 92-run win and India's 3-0 series sweep over Zimbabwe.
articles.nri_angle: India's women completed a dominant home sweep with record power-hitting — 128 sixes in 2026, 50 clear of the next team — a benchmark diaspora fans can measure the side's T20 ambitions against.

articles.title: Nishad Kumar's Double Gold Headlines India's Five-Gold Day at Asian Para Games
articles.excerpt: Kumar cleared a Games-record 2.04m in the high jump T47 a day after winning the long jump, as India's tally at Aichi-Nagoya rose to 35 medals with athletics delivering all five of Tuesday's golds.
articles.image_caption: Nishad Kumar, pictured in September 2024. The para athlete won double gold as India took five golds at the Asian Para Games.
articles.nri_angle: India's para-athletes, led by Nishad Kumar's historic double, are building the depth diaspora fans saw emerge at Paris 2024 — with LA 2028 quota places already being banked.

articles.title: Chinmay Sutar Hits Unbeaten 400, Only Second Indian to Reach the Mark
articles.excerpt: The Mizoram batter made 400 not out off 517 balls against Nagaland in Sovima, passing Prithvi Shaw's 379 and finishing behind only B. B. Nimbalkar's 443 not out in Ranji Trophy history.
